title: Migration Guard expected result
description: Machine-checkable expectations for one test case. Consumed by scripts/evaluate_reports.py. Severity semantics are frozen in CONTRIBUTING.md; 'critical: true' is redundant with severity == BLOCKER and exists so that the evaluator can assert consistency.

kind.$comment: positive = the migration has risk that must be found. negative = the migration is safe and must not be reported as risky.

allowed_verdicts.$comment: Verdict accuracy counts a run as correct only when its verdict is in this list. Keep it as tight as the severity rules allow; add a second value only when a defensible reading exists.

forbidden_findings.$comment: Categories that must NOT appear in the agent report. Used for false-positive control.

required_unknowns.$comment: Facts the report must list under Unknowns because the case deliberately withholds them.

destructive.$comment: Deprecated. True when the migration contains an irreversible step (data cannot be restored). The report must then state an approval to accept risk and a recovery plan. Use `irreversible`.

irreversible.$comment: True when the migration loses or overwrites data that cannot be restored without a backup. Separate from `destructive`, which only described the shape of the statement. The validator requires a statement in migration.sql that removes stored data (DROP TABLE, DROP COLUMN, TRUNCATE, DELETE FROM), unless `irreversible_reason` explains why the loss comes from a step the file does not contain.

irreversible_reason.$comment: Why the case is irreversible when migration.sql itself contains no removing statement, e.g. the later step of an expand-and-contract plan. Required to be meaningful (at least 20 characters) and forbidden when `irreversible` is false or absent.

id.$comment: Stable identifier local to the case, e.g. F1.

must_cite_evidence.$comment: Each entry is a file path (optionally with :line) that the evidence in the expected.md quotes. The evaluator checks that the cited path appears in the report and that the report cites it near the finding.

must_mention_any.$comment: At least one of these strings (case-insensitive substring) must appear in the finding text. Encodes the core concept the finding must convey.

requires_human_approval.$comment: Deprecated. True only when an approval to accept risk is required. Prefer `approval`.

approval.$comment: Approval class required for this finding, decided by reversibility, not by operation type. `none` = reversible and additive. `schedule` = reversible but costly (window/throttle). `accept-risk` = the previous value cannot be restored.

reversible.$comment: True when the previous value or structure can be restored without a backup.

max_severity_if_present.$comment: If the category does appear, its severity must not exceed this level.
